title: Coefficients and sites
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The *coefficient stages* are
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with constructibility, finite Tor
amplitude, constructible intervals and Tate twists. The integral, rational and algebraically closed coefficient conventions are those of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. On schemes where $\ell$ is invertible, their finite Tor conventions are [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and Tate twists have the domain and coefficient conventions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. At a finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, for a
scheme $X$, $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of the derived category
of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] consisting of the
bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes],
$D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ consists of those objects $K$ of finite Tor
amplitude: there exist integers $u\leq v$ such that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[u,v]$ in the sense of [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. At this finite stage, for integers $u\leq v$, $D_c^{[u,v]}(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ of objects with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[u,v]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The constant complex $\Lambda_X$ is the constant sheaf $\Lambda$
placed in degree $0$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], the unit of $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ [def-kun-derived-tensor].
Morphisms are separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: The unit assertion is elementary from the constructions. Write $R=\Lambda_X$ for the constant ring sheaf and $R[0]$ for its degree-zero complex [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. For any complex $C$, the total tensor construction [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives chain isomorphisms $R[0]\otimes_R C\cong C$ and $C\otimes_R R[0]\cong C$: on local pure tensors they are $r\otimes c\mapsto rc$ and $c\otimes r\mapsto rc$, with inverses $c\mapsto1\otimes c$ and $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. For each site object $U$ and degree $i$, balancing gives $r\otimes c=1\otimes rc$ in $R(U)\otimes_{R(U)}C^i(U)$ and $c\otimes r=rc\otimes1$ in $C^i(U)\otimes_{R(U)}R(U)$. The displayed maps and inverses commute with restrictions, so these presheaf isomorphisms sheafify to the sheaf tensor isomorphisms by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The total differential is the original differential of $C$: on the left its only summand has $p=0$, hence sign $+1$, and on the right $d_R=0$ makes the signed second term vanish. Consequently tensoring an acyclic complex with $R[0]$ is acyclic, so $R[0]$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $K$ in the derived category choose a representing complex $C$ with $Q(C)\cong K$, where $Q$ is the localization functor. In [def-kun-derived-tensor] use $R[0]$ itself as the K-flat first argument to compute $R[0]\otimes_R^L K$ by $R[0]\otimes_R C$. For $K\otimes_R^L R[0]$, choose a K-flat resolution $P\to C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},R)$ and compute by $P\otimes_R R[0]$. The displayed chain isomorphisms identify the resulting objects with $Q(C)\cong K$ and $Q(P)\cong Q(C)\cong K$, respectively; the middle isomorphism comes from inverting the quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ in the localization. Thus the defined constant complex is the tensor unit. For a chain map $f:C\to C'$, $f(rc)=rf(c)$ makes both multiplication squares commute in each degree. These squares still commute after $Q$, and a square with a quasi-isomorphism still commutes after inverting that map. Thus they also commute for the roofs representing derived morphisms, giving natural unit identifications on the derived category.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. The admissible coefficient rings are
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, regarded as condensed rings: $A_{E,n}$ with its
discrete topology, $\underline{\mathcal O}_E$ and $\underline E$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), and
$\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]). For a scheme $X$ the coefficient sheaf is
$\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ ([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]); it is the
unit of $\otimes^L_{\Lambda}$, and $D(X,\Lambda)=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is the derived
category of $\Lambda_X$-modules ([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]). $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\subseteq
D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ consists of the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology
sheaves ([sk-def-sfb-constructible], [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), and
$D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ of those of finite Tor amplitude over
$\Lambda_X$. These categories come with constructible intervals and the Tate twists of
[sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. Morphisms are separated of finite type.

*Finite coefficients.* For $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ the sheaf $A_X$ is the classical constant sheaf, and
$\nu_X^*$ identifies the étale categories with the pro-étale ones: $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$,
the bounded complexes of sheaves of $A$-modules on the small étale site with constructible
cohomology sheaves, and its subcategory $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$, are carried
equivalently onto $D^b_c(X,A)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ ([sk-prop-sf-comparison],
[sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison], [sk-cor-pe-finite-tor-comparison]). Finite-level
arguments may therefore be carried out on the small étale site.

*Integral and rational coefficients.* For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ the categories
$D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ are the full subcategories of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ just defined,
and no other model of them is used. The pulled-back rings satisfy
$\mathcal O_{E,X}\cong\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$, $E_X\cong\mathcal O_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ and
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\cong\varinjlim_EE_X$ ([sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]); these are
theorems about the condensed rings, not definitions. The following consequences are used in
proofs to reduce to finite levels.

1. A complex $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ lies in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ if and
   only if it is derived $\pi_E$-complete and $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_{E,1})_X$
   is in $D^b_c(X,A_{E,1})$; then every reduction
   $K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X$ is in $D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})$, with
   cohomology in one interval independent of $n$, and $K\simeq R\varprojlim_nK_n$
   ([sk-prop-integral-criterion], [det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions]).
2. Extension of scalars along $\mathcal O_{E,X}\to E_X$ identifies $D^b_c(X,E)$ with the
   category obtained from $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by tensoring the Hom groups with $E$; in
   particular every object of $D^b_c(X,E)$ has an integral model
   ([sk-thm-sfb-rationalization-comparison]).
3. Every object and every morphism of $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ is obtained by extension of scalars
   from some finite $E$, so that $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)\simeq2\text{-}\varinjlim_ED^b_c(X,E)$
   ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]).

For these three coefficient rings, finite Tor amplitude is automatic:
$D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)=D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ ([det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc]).
